text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak warns Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the serious consequences of settlements, and asks him not to be too confident. Mubarak says that peace will continue with or without Netanyahu and says that if he were in the prime minister's place he would resign.

- Mubarak receives a letter from United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan about the latest developments in the region, and gets an invitation from the Romanian president to visit Romania.
- Mubarak calls U.S. President Bill Clinton by telephone to wish him well, after Clinton fell and injured his knee.
- Minister of Supply and Trade Ahmed Gueily says Egypt will not sign any partnership agreement with the European Union unless it is in Egypt's interests and achieves a balanced trade relationship.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to come to Cairo in the next few days and meet Mubarak.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri is to head a delegation to China, Malaysia and Singapore to sign agreements and discuss increasing Egyptian exports and economic ties, and setting up joint private sector projects.
- EgyptAir decides to set up a new route between Kuwait, Hurghada and Sharm el-Sheikh.
- Cabinet is to discuss the results of President Mubarak's visit to Washington, Paris and Morocco.
